title: Japan trading unit corrected to one unit
summary: J-REITs trade in single units; the platform had assumed lots of 100. Positions in Japan can now be sized and trimmed in steps of about 0.02% of NAV instead of about 0.8%.

title: Purchases and sales netted within each Track A cycle
summary: Until this date a Track A cycle could buy a position and sell it again in the same run when the purchase took the portfolio over a cap. Each cycle's purchases and sales are now netted before anything trades. This ended same-day round trips. It did not change how cap breaches are resolved, and sales forced by caps continued.

title: Track A weekly portfolio review restored
summary: The weekly review returned no decisions on 16 and 23 August because its response was cut short, and the run reported success. The limit was raised. From this date the review can again propose sales on investment grounds.

title: Seven-day minimum between memos on the same name
summary: A new filing could trigger a fresh memo on a name every day, which crowded other names out of the memo flow. A name is now eligible for a new memo no sooner than seven days after its last.

title: Language model changed
summary: The model behind the specialist, reviewer and Track A agents changed from Claude Sonnet 4.6 to Claude Sonnet 5.5. Decisions from this date were made on the new model.

title: Quarterly reporting rebuilt
summary: The quarterly report generator was rebuilt after the first run on 14 October produced figures that were wrong or not comparable. Results are now measured on NAV at the period end, against a total-return benchmark, and a closed quarter gives the same figures whenever it is run. The 14 October version of the 2026Q3 report is withdrawn and replaced by this one; it remains in the repository history.

title: Cost-to-trade test on Track A switches
summary: When a Track A cycle's purchases breached a cap, a holding could be sold to make room whatever the difference in expected return, at a cost of 0.5% of the amount switched. A sale of a holding to fund a new purchase now stands only if the purchase's expected return, measured against its own market, exceeds the holding's by more than 2.5 points a year (METHODOLOGY 5.1). Otherwise the purchase is rejected and the holding kept. The Track A prompts were updated to describe the rule.

title: Held names refreshed from their last reviewed memo
summary: A held name is due a new memo 21 days after its last. A memo that failed review counted as a refresh, so a name whose memos kept failing could go more than a month without a usable one. The 21 days now run from the last memo that passed review.

title: Memo format check accepts a scenario labelled 'id'
summary: Some analyst outputs since October labelled each scenario 'id' where the memo format requires 'name', and were discarded before review. 29 outputs failed the format check from October to 21 November, most of them for this reason. They are now read. The analyst's instructions are unchanged.

title: Prompt version recorded with each decision
summary: Each decision was meant to carry the version of the prompt it was made under. A defect left the field empty on every decision before this date. It is now recorded. Only the first version of each prompt existed before this date.

title: A memo marked "revise" at review is revised once and reviewed again
summary: A memo the reviewer marks "revise" is now revised once by the analyst, in words only, and reviewed again; only "reject" fails. Conviction, the gates and every number are restored in code after the revision. Before, "revise" failed the memo and nothing was returned to the analyst: 37 of 548 memos had failed review (METHODOLOGY 7.3).

title: Track B decision records: country and sector weights after make-room sales
summary: Decisions that sell part or all of a holding to make room for a purchase now record country and sector weights after the sale. Earlier records overstated those two weights; see corrections/2026-11-28-ic-post-decision-exposures.md. Holdings and performance were not affected.
